_about: What each check stands on, in the order it is looked for: the editor's documentation, public reports, a local test. A level left out is not claimed. Measured precision is in precision.json.

01-claude-md-case.documented_note: The memory page names CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md and says nothing about case (read 2026-10-08).
01-claude-md-case.reported_note: Users report the lowercase file is found on macOS and Windows (case-insensitive filesystems) and not on Linux.

tested.how: A codeword in claude.md, then in CLAUDE.md; a session asked for it without reading files.

01-claude-md-case.precision_note: 44 of 46 findings were instruction files that Linux does not load; 2 were a personal cheatsheet and user documentation. 44 public repositories, 2026-10-08, labelled by the assistant, not blind.

23-agent-tools.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents (an Agent(...) list applies only to an agent run as the main thread)
23-agent-tools.documented_note: The alias Task -> Agent was documented on the sub-agents page and is no longer (read 2026-10-08). tools-reference lists TaskOutput as "Removed in v2.1.277" (read 2026-10-17).

tested.how: deny ["Task"], deny ["Agent"] and no rule, each in a fresh project; a session asked to spawn a subagent.
tested.result: Task and Agent rules both remove the Agent tool; without a rule the subagent runs.

tested_taskoutput.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project in an empty git repository holding .claude/agents/shop-reader.md, asked to call the Agent tool with that subagent; three agents: tools: TaskOutput / tools: Read, TaskOutput / tools: Read, Grep. One run each.
tested_taskoutput.result: tools: TaskOutput: "Agent 'shop-reader' would be spawned with zero tools — refusing. Its tools list resolved to nothing: unrecognized [TaskOutput]." tools: Read, TaskOutput: the agent listed Read alone. tools: Read, Grep: Read and Grep.

43-mcp-credential-var.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp (Credential variables that read as empty: five names, given as examples)
43-mcp-credential-var.documented_note: The page lists ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, HTTPS_PROXY and NPM_TOKEN after "such as"; the other eight names the check matches are measured, not documented.

tested.how: claude mcp list with a disposable CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, against a local HTTP server that logs the headers it receives; each name set and unset, with and without :-default.
tested.result: AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS and NODE_AUTH_TOKEN arrive empty in every case; AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN and a name of the project's own expand, and :-DEF gives DEF.

42-permissions-rule.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes (auto mode drops `Agent` allow rules); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (the Manual-mode table does not list the Agent tool among those that ask; Agent(<name>) rules are described for deny, parameter rules for deny and ask)
42-permissions-rule.documented_note: Scope of this entry: the NOTICE on a whole-tool Agent allow rule ("Agent", "Agent(*)"). The other 42-permissions-rule findings cite the permissions page directly. Read 2026-10-09. Also the `$HOME` advice: the permissions page names `//`, `~/`, `/` and relative paths, and no variable.

tested.how: claude -p with --setting-sources "" (no permission rule at all), in default and in dontAsk mode, asked to delegate to a sub-agent; then the same with --disallowedTools "Agent(general-purpose)".
tested.result: Without any rule the Agent tool was called, the sub-agent started and answered, permission_denials empty, in both modes. With the deny rule the call was refused: "Agent type 'general-purpose' has been denied by permission rule".

tested_home_variable.how: claude -p --model claude-haiku-5-5 --setting-sources project --settings <file>, HOME set to a temporary folder holding probe/secret.txt (also the working directory), asked to Read that file; three settings files: no rule, deny Read($HOME/probe/secret.txt), deny Read(~/probe/secret.txt). One run each.
tested_home_variable.result: No rule: the content was returned. Deny Read($HOME/...): the content was returned, permission_denials empty. Deny Read(~/...): refused, "File is in a directory that is denied by your permission settings."

tested_mid_colon_star.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --allowedTools Bash --debug-file, project settings holding one deny rule, asked to run one command. Rules and commands: Bash(git:* status) vs `git status` and `git -C . status`; Bash(echo:* hello) vs `echo:x hello`; Bash(git status) vs `git status` (control). One run each.
tested_mid_colon_star.result: Bash(git:* status): both git commands ran, permission_denials empty (the debug log shows the rule added to projectSettings). Bash(echo:* hello): `echo:x hello` denied. Control denied. No startup warning about the pattern in the -p debug log. The colon is literal, `*` a wildcard, as the permissions page says.

35-hooks-shape.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (Block the action when a hook fails; command and HTTP hook fields)
35-hooks-shape.documented_note: onFailure: "continue" (default) or "block", on command and http hooks, 2.1.295+; no effect on Stop, SubagentStop, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle nor on async/asyncRewake command hooks (read 2026-10-17). Scope of this entry: the onFailure NOTICEs (tested) and the `hooks: []` NOTICE of a skill's frontmatter (tested_skill_hooks_empty).

tested.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --allowedTools Bash, a PreToolUse Bash command hook running `node <missing>.js` (exec form, timeout 10), with and without "onFailure": "block"; asked to run `ls`. One run each.
tested.result: With block: the call was refused, "PreToolUse:Bash hook error: [node .../missing-check.js]: failed; blocking because onFailure is \"block\"". Without: `ls` ran. The no-effect cases (Stop, async) were not tested.

tested_skill_hooks_empty.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools Skill, from an empty temporary git repository holding .claude/skills/shop-orders/SKILL.md (frontmatter name, description, `hooks: []`; body: reply with a marker word) and a control skill without `hooks`; asked to call the Skill tool with shop-orders and reply what it says. Read from the stream: init.skills, the Skill tool_use and its tool_result, the final reply. One run. Replayed by probes/run_probes.py (--only 35-hooks-shape).
tested_skill_hooks_empty.result: shop-orders is in init.skills, beside the control; the Skill call returned no error and the reply was the body's marker word. Scope: a skill only; an agent's `hooks: []` was not run.

35-hooks-matcher.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (Matcher patterns: only letters, digits, _, -, spaces, `,` and `|` make an exact list; any other character makes the whole matcher one JavaScript regular expression on the tool name; argument patterns go in `if`)
35-hooks-matcher.documented_note: Scope of this entry: a permission rule written as one `|` alternative of a matcher (NOTICE when the matcher is a valid regular expression, ERROR when it is not). The page does not say what an invalid regular expression does; that part is measured only.

tested.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools Bash Write, in two empty temporary git repositories. Each .claude/settings.json has two PreToolUse command hooks that append the hook input's tool_name to a log in the repository: the probed matcher, and a control matcher `Bash|Write`. Probed matchers: `Bash(git *)|Write` (a valid regular expression), `Write|Edit(*.ts)` (not one). Asked to run `git status` with Bash, then create note.txt with Write. One run each. Replayed by probes/run_probes.py.
tested.result: `Bash(git *)|Write`: fired on Write only, not on the `git status` Bash call. `Write|Edit(*.ts)`: fired on nothing. The control fired on Bash and Write in both repositories, so an invalid matcher does not stop the other groups of the same event.

43-mcp-shape.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp (Claude Code skips a "type": "sdk" entry in .mcp.json, ~/.claude.json, or settings)
43-mcp-shape.documented_note: Read 2026-10-17. Scope of this entry: the `type: sdk` ERROR.

tested.how: `claude mcp list` in an empty git repository whose .mcp.json holds a type sdk server and a stdio server; output filtered to those two names.
tested.result: "[Warning] [shop-sdk] mcpServers.shop-sdk: Skipped — MCP server \"shop-sdk\" declares type \"sdk\", which only an SDK host application can register"; the stdio server listed, pending approval.

44-plugin-path.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference (Fields; Path rules: every component path starts with ./ and stays inside the root)
44-plugin-path.documented_note: Read 2026-10-17: workflows, experimental.themes, experimental.monitors and top-level themes/monitors are component paths; experimental.evals is not. Scope of this entry: those keys, added in 0.26.0.

tested.how: claude plugin validate on a minimal plugin, plugin.json varied: experimental.themes "themes/"; monitors "./../shared/monitors.json"; workflows ["workflows/refund.js"]; experimental.themes "./themes/" (control).
tested.result: "experimental.themes: Invalid string: must start with \"./\""; "monitors: Path contains \"..\" which could be a path traversal attempt" plus a warning to declare it under experimental.monitors; "workflows.0: Invalid string: must start with \"./\""; the control passed.

manual-rule-guards-creation.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (A path-scoped rule loads when Claude uses the Read, Write, or Edit tool on a matching file, or views it with a Bash command that counts as a read)
manual-rule-guards-creation.documented_note: Read 2026-10-17. Not an audit.py check: the [MANUAL] checklist item and anti-pattern F4. The changelog dates the Write/Edit trigger to 2.1.288 and the Bash one to 2.1.293.
manual-rule-guards-creation.reported_note: Reported upstream on 2.1.280 (#93248): creating a file did not load the rule. Not measured here on 2.1.280; the only local run is the tested entry, on 2.1.302.

tested.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --permission-mode acceptEdits, a rule .claude/rules/api.md with paths src/api/** and an InstructionsLoaded hook appending each event to a log. Three runs: Write creating src/api/refunds.ts with no prior read; Bash `cat src/api/existing.ts`; Write creating src/web/other.ts (control).
tested.result: Write in scope: the log shows .claude/rules/api.md, load_reason path_glob_match, and the model said the rule arrived in the Write's tool result, after the file was written. cat: same log line. Control: nothing loaded.

frontmatter-bom.documented_note: Not an audit.py check of its own: the frontmatter readers used by 02-skill-frontmatter, 08-agent-frontmatter, 19-frontmatter-quoting, 22-rule-glob-match and the frontmatter hooks of 35-hooks-shape skip a UTF-8 byte order mark before the opening `---` since 0.26.0. The skills, sub-agents and memory pages were not found to mention a byte order mark (audit relecture, 2026-10-17); not re-read for this entry.

tested.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools Read, from an empty temporary git repository. Files opening with a byte order mark, each beside a twin without one: skill shop-refunds (description with a marker word, body with another), skill shop-coupons with `user-invocable: false` (twin shop-discounts), agent file shop-reviewer.md with frontmatter name shop-reviewer-bom (twin shop-tester-plain), rule payments.md with paths src/payments/** (twin web.md with src/web/**), plus an unconditional rule and an InstructionsLoaded command hook logging file_path and load_reason. Asked to Read src/web/page.ts, then src/payments/amount.ts, then quote the description of shop-refunds from its skills listing without another tool. Read from the stream: init.skills, init.agents, tool_use; from the hook log: each load. One run. Replayed by probes/run_probes.py (--only frontmatter-bom).
tested.result: Skill with a mark: in init.skills, and the reply quoted its frontmatter description exactly, marker included, without the body's marker and without reading the file (the model's own account). Skill with a mark and `user-invocable: false`: left out of init.skills, as its twin without a mark: the field was read. Agent with a mark: in init.agents under its frontmatter name. Rule with a mark: loaded only on reading src/payments/amount.ts (load_reason path_glob_match), not at session start, like its twin on src/web/page.ts; the unconditional rule and CLAUDE.md loaded at session_start. Side observation, not used as a signal: `disable-model-invocation: true` left a skill in init.skills, with or without a mark.

01-claude-md-import-syntax.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Import additional files: "Relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, not the working directory. Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of four hops."; "Without the backslashes, the path ends at the first space"; "A path wrapped in quotes isn't imported at all"; "Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks.")
01-claude-md-import-syntax.documented_note: Read 2026-10-17. Scope: what the auditor counts as an `@path` import (parsing/markdown.py import_tokens), shared by 17-always-loaded-budget, 01-claude-md-import (now on every file of the import walk, repo.walk_imports) and the NOTICE 01-claude-md-import-syntax. The page does not say what punctuation next to a path does; that part is measured only.

tested.how: claude -p 'Reply with the single word OK.' --model haiku --setting-sources project --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config, from an empty temporary git repository whose .claude/settings.json has an InstructionsLoaded command hook appending each event (file_path, load_reason) to a log. CLAUDE.md holds one paragraph per form, each naming its own file under docs/ (all files exist): `@docs/space.md` followed by a space; at a line end; at the end of the file with no newline; followed by `:`, `,`, `.`, `"`, `;`, `!`, `?`, `)`; `@docs/colonfile.md:` and `@docs/commafile.md,` beside files literally named `docs/colonfile.md:` and `docs/commafile.md,`; preceded by `(`, `"`, `'`, a lone backtick, a word character (`shop@docs/...`); wrapped in double quotes; in a code span; in a fenced block; `@./docs/dotrel.md`; `@docs/slash.md/` (a file, trailing slash); `@docs/folder/` (a folder holding inner.md); `@docs/NOTES` (no extension). Plus a chain CLAUDE.md -> docs/h1.md -> h2 -> ... -> h6, each written relative to the importing file (`@h2.md` inside docs/h1.md), and in docs/h1.md `@docs/rootrel.md`, a file that exists only relative to the repository root. One run, cost $0.0018. `@~/` was not probed (it would read the home folder). An earlier run the same day (same flags, one run) had loaded only `@docs/plain.md` out of `@docs/plain.md`, `@docs/colon.md:`, `@docs/comma.md,`, `@docs/period.md.` and `(@docs/paren.md)`. Replayed by probes/run_probes.py (--only 01-claude-md-import-syntax).
tested.result: Loaded (load_reason include): space after, line end, end of file, `@./docs/dotrel.md`, `@docs/slash.md/` (as docs/slash.md), `@docs/NOTES` (no extension), and the chain docs/h1.md to docs/h4.md. Not loaded: `:`, `,`, `.`, `"`, `;`, `!`, `?` or `)` right after the path - nor the files named with the `:` or `,`, so the character is not read as part of the path; `(`, `"`, `'`, a lone backtick or a word character right before the `@`, so in `(@docs/paren.md)` each parenthesis alone is enough; double quotes around it; code span; fenced block; `@docs/folder/`; docs/h5.md and docs/h6.md (the fifth hop: the four-hop limit holds); docs/rootrel.md (no fallback to the repository root). Not probed: any other character next to a path (`*`, `[`, `]`, `>`, `|`, `-`, ...), `@~/`, an absolute path, a folder of the same name as a file.
